Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 1:

Surah Hud [Makkiyya (Meccan) except verses 12, 17 and 114, which are Madaniyya (Medinan); its verses number 123. It was revealed after Surah Yunus.]

﴿Alif. Lam. Ra.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by this. ﴿This is a Book whose verses have been made firm﴾ in wondrous arrangement and exquisite meanings, ﴿then elaborated﴾ explained through the rulings, the narratives and the admonitions, ﴿from One who is All-Wise, All-Aware﴾, that is, Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 2:

﴿Alif﴾ i.e., that ﴿do not worship except Allah. Indeed I am a warner to you from Him﴾ of the punishment if you disbelieve, ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾ of the reward if you believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 3:

﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾ from shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿then repent to Him﴾ return to Him ﴿with obedience﴾; ﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision﴾ in the world, ﴿a good enjoyment﴾ with a pleasant life and abundance of provision, ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is death. ﴿And He will give every person of merit﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿his merit﴾ in deeds, ﴿His reward﴾. ﴿But if you turn away﴾ here there is an omission of one of the two tā' (i.e., the verb is originally tatawallaw), meaning you turn away, ﴿then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection.
Qur'anic quotation: ﴿To Allah is your return, and He is over all things Competent.﴾ Commentary: From Him comes the reward and the punishment.

It was revealed, as al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning those who were shy to relieve themselves or to have intercourse, so they would bend their backs (to avoid being seen by the sky). It was also said that it was revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿Behold, they fold their breasts that they may hide from Him﴾, i.e., from Allah. ﴿Behold, when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, wrapping themselves in them. ﴿He knows what they conceal and what they reveal﴾, exalted is He, so their hiding is of no avail. ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is in the breasts﴾, i.e., of what is in the hearts.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 6:

﴿And there is not⟩ [the word] "min" is superfluous. ﴿any creature (dabba) on the earth⟩ it is whatever crawls upon it. ﴿but upon Allah is its provision⟩ He has undertaken it, by His grace, exalted is He. ﴿And He knows its place of rest⟩ its dwelling in the world, or its loins (al-sulb). ﴿and its place of storage⟩ after death, or in the womb (al-rahm). ﴿All⟩ of what has been mentioned ﴿is in a Clear Book⟩ clear, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 7:

﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾ — the first of them Sunday and the last of them Friday — ﴿and His Throne was over the water﴾ before their creation, ﴿and He was over the wind﴾ [i.e., the water was upon the back of the wind] ﴿so that He might test you﴾ — this is connected to "created": that is, He created them and what is in them of benefits and interests for you, in order to test you ﴿as to which of you is best in deed﴾, i.e., most obedient to Allah. ﴿And if you say﴾, O Muhammad, to them, ﴿that you will be resurrected after death, those who disbelieve will surely say: "This is not﴾ — what ﴿this﴾ is — the Qur'an which speaks of the Resurrection, or what you are saying — ﴿but clear magic.﴾ Clear, evident. In another reading it is "a magician" (sāḥir), and the one referred to is the Prophet (ﷺ).

And if We postpone the punishment from them until a limited number of times (ummah, here meaning a period of time), they will surely say, mockingly: "What is holding it back?" (ma yahbisuhu, i.e., what prevents it from descending?) "Is it not that on the day it comes to them, it will not be turned away" (masrufan, i.e., repelled) "from them, and there will befall them" (haqa, i.e., descended upon them) "that at which they used to mock," (i.e., of the punishment).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 11, verse 9:

﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us﴾ [i.e., the disbelieving man] ﴿wealth and health﴾ ﴿then We withdraw it from him, indeed he is despairing﴾ [i.e., despairing] ﴿ungrateful﴾ [i.e., extremely disbelieving] ﴿of Allah's mercy﴾ ﴿ungrateful﴾ [i.e., extremely ungrateful] ﴿toward Him﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 10:

﴿And if We let him taste blessing after adversity that had touched him,﴾ meaning poverty and hardship, ﴿he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me,"﴾ meaning the calamities, and he did not expect their removal, nor does he give thanks for them. ﴿Indeed, he is exultant﴾ meaning exultant in insolence, ﴿and boastful﴾ over the people because of what he has been given.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 11:

﴿Except﴾ (i.e., but) ﴿those who are patient﴾ in adversity ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ in ease, ﴿those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ which is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 12:

﴿Perhaps﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿you will leave out some of what is revealed to you﴾, so that you do not convey it to them because of their indifference to it, ﴿and your breast will be constricted by it﴾ at reciting it to them, ﴿lest they say: "Why has not a treasure been sent down to him, or an angel come with him"﴾ to confirm him, as we have suggested, ﴿You are only a warner﴾; so your duty is only to convey, not to bring what they have proposed. ﴿And God is Guardian over everything﴾, watchful, and He will recompense them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 13:

﴿Am﴾ (rather) ﴿they say, "He has invented it."﴾ That is, the Qur'an. ﴿Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it [in eloquence and rhetoric], invented,"﴾ for you are Arabs, eloquent like me. He challenged them with this first, then with a single surah. ﴿And call upon﴾ for assistance in that ﴿whomever you can, besides Allah﴾ that is, other than Him, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in claiming that it is invented.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 14:

﴿Then if﴾ they do not respond to you, [i.e., those whom you have called upon for help], ﴿then know﴾ [this is an address to the polytheists], ﴿that it has been sent down﴾ [sent down] ﴿with the knowledge of Allah﴾ [i.e., accompanied by it], and it is not a fabrication against Him, ﴿and that﴾ [an-, lightened (mukhaffafah), i.e., that it is] ﴿there is no god but Him. So will you then submit?﴾ [i.e., become Muslims] after this decisive proof.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 15:

﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾ by persisting in polytheism (shirk). It is said that it refers to those who do deeds to be seen by others (al-murā'un, the showing-off hypocrites). ﴿We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾, i.e., the recompense for the good they did, such as charity and maintaining ties of kinship. ﴿Therein﴾ by Us expanding their provision for them. ﴿And they therein﴾, i.e., in this world, ﴿will not be deprived﴾, i.e., will not be diminished in anything.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 16:

﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire; and what they did [in the world] will come to nothing﴾ [i.e., became void, بَطَلَ] ﴿and what they used to do﴾ [i.e., what they did, ما صَنَعُوهُ] ﴿therein﴾ [i.e., in the Hereafter]; so there is no reward for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 17:

﴿Is he who stands upon a clear proof (bayyina) from his Lord﴾ — bayan (clarification) — and he is the Prophet (ﷺ), or the believers; and it is the Qur'an. ﴿And there follows him﴾ — yatba'uhu (follows him) — ﴿a witness﴾ — shahid — testifying to his truthfulness ﴿from Him﴾ — that is, from Allah, and he is Jibril. ﴿And before him﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿was the Book of Musa﴾ — the Torah — a witness for it also, ﴿as a guide and a mercy﴾ — a state (hal). Is it like one who is not so? No. ﴿Those﴾ — that is, he who stands upon a clear proof — ﴿believe in it﴾ — that is, in the Qur'an — so for them is the Garden. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾ — all the disbelievers — ﴿then the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt﴾ — shakk (doubt) — ﴿about it﴾ — about the Qur'an — ﴿indeed it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people﴾ — that is, the people of Makkah — ﴿do not believe.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 18:

﴿Who is more unjust﴾ than one who ﴿fabricates a lie against God﴾, i.e., there is no one more unjust, by attributing to Him a partner and a son. ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, among the whole of creation. ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾ (al-ashhad, the plural of shahid, "witness," and they are the angels, who will bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed the message, and against the disbelievers that they denied it): ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers﴾, meaning the polytheists.

Those who bar from the way of Allah: the religion of Islam, and seek to make it crooked: seeking the way to be crooked. And they, concerning the Hereafter, they are (disbelievers): an emphatic restatement.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 20:

﴿Those will not be able to escape¹ [Allah] upon the earth, and they will have no protectors other than Allah﴾ — i.e., other than Him — ﴿who could protect them from His punishment⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ —

Note: the Arabic term "awliya'" here is rendered as "protectors" (helpers, supporters).

﴿Their punishment will be doubled﴾ — because of their misguiding others. ﴿They could not bear to hear﴾ the truth ﴿and they used not to see﴾ — i.e., because of their intense aversion to it, as if they were unable to do that.

Those are the ones who have lost their souls (﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسهمْ﴾), because of their destiny to the eternal Fire upon them. ﴿And what they used to fabricate﴾ (﴿وضَلَّ﴾) vanished (غابَ) from them (﴿عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾), against Allah, of the claim of a partner (مِن دَعْوى الشَّرِيك).
﴿Lā jaram﴾ — truly, certainly.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 23:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves⁠ before their Lord﴾ [they] settled down, found tranquility, or turned back in repentance (to their Lord).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 24:

﴿Mathal﴾ (the description) of ﴿the two groups﴾, the disbelievers and the believers, ﴿is like the blind and the deaf﴾: this is the example of the disbeliever, ﴿and the seeing and the hearing﴾: this is the example of the believer. ﴿Are the two equal in comparison?﴾ No. ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ In it, the ta' in the original (tatadhakkarun) is assimilated into the dhal, meaning: "will you not be admonished?"

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner."﴾ That is, bi-anni (أَنِّي, "that I"). In one qira'ah (recitation variant) it is read with a kasra (the vowel i) as إنِّي, with the verb of saying omitted (ḥadhf al-qawl), meaning "[saying] indeed I..." ﴿to you a clear warner﴾, clear in warning.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 11, verse 26:

﴿An﴾ i.e., that ﴿do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you﴾ if you worship other than Him ﴿the punishment of a painful day﴾ painful, in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 27:

﴿So the chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said﴾, and they were the nobles, ﴿"We see you only as a human being like ourselves"﴾, meaning, you have no superiority over us, ﴿"And we see none following you except those who are our lowest (arādhilunā)"﴾, meaning our lowest ones, like the weavers (al-ḥākah) and the cobblers (al-asākifah), ﴿"at first glance (bādi' al-ra'y)"﴾, which may be read with a hamza or without it, meaning, an initial judgment made without reflection upon you. Its being in the accusative is as an adverb of time, meaning, at the time of the first occurrence of their opinion. ﴿"And we see for you no merit over us"﴾, by which you would deserve to be followed by us. ﴿"Rather, we think you are liars"﴾, in your claim of prophethood. They included his people along with him in the address.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 28:

﴿He said: "O my people! Tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself"﴾ — i.e., prophethood — ﴿but it has been made obscure to you﴾ — i.e., it has been hidden from you. In another reading, it is recited with the letter mim doubled and in the passive form (fa-ʻummiyat), ﴿shall we compel you to accept it﴾ — i.e., shall we force you to accept it — ﴿while you are averse to it?﴾ — i.e., we are not able to do that.

O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return for it (for conveying the message). My reward is only from God. And I will not drive away those who have believed, as you have asked me to do. Indeed, they will meet their Lord (through resurrection), and He will recompense them and take their right from those who wronged them and drove them out. But I see you as a people who are ignorant (of the outcome of your affair).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 30:

﴿And O my people, who would help me⦅yamna'uni⦆ against God﴾, meaning, who would protect me⦅yamna'uni⦆ from God, ﴿that is, from His punishment﴾, ﴿if I drive them away﴾, meaning, I would have no helper. ﴿Will you not then⦅afalā⦆ remember﴾, meaning, why will you not take heed? The verb تَذَكَّرُونَ (tadhakkarūna), originally with two tā' sounds, has the second tā' assimilated (idgham) into the dhāl, so that it is read with a doubled dhāl, meaning "you take admonition."

﴿I do not tell you that the treasures of God are with me, nor﴾ that I ﴿know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, but rather I am a human being like you. ﴿Nor do I say of those whom your eyes despise﴾ (scorn) ﴿that God will never give them any good. God knows best what is in their souls﴾ (their hearts). ﴿Indeed, then I would be﴾ (if I said that) [a wrongdoer].

﴿They said, "O Noah, you have argued with us and multiplied your arguments with us, so bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful."﴾

(They said, "O Noah, you have argued with us") disputed with us, ﴿and multiplied your arguments with us﴾ so you have multiplied our disputation, ﴿so bring us what you threaten us with﴾ of punishment, ﴿if you are among the truthful﴾ about it.
﴿He said: "Only Allah will bring it to you, if He wills, [meaning] His hastening it for you, for His command is to Him, not to me. And you cannot escape"﴾ by escaping Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 34:

﴿And my advice will not benefit you, even if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to lead you astray﴾ meaning, your misguidance. The response of the condition is indicated by what precedes it: ﴿my advice will not benefit you﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 35:

﴿Am﴾ (rather) ﴿yaqooloona﴾ (say), i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿ftaraahu﴾ ("he has invented it"), i.e., Muhammad has fabricated the Qur'an. ﴿Qul in iftaraytahu fa'alayya ijraami﴾ ("Say: If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime"), i.e., my sin, meaning its punishment. ﴿Wa ana bari'un mimma tujrimoon﴾ ("and I am innocent of what you commit"), i.e., of your crime in attributing the fabrication to me.

And it was revealed to Noah: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed [tabta'is, i.e., do not grieve] at what they have been doing" — [that is, of] associating partners with God. Thereupon he invoked [a curse] against them, saying: "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers [who dwell upon it]" — and so on — and God answered his supplication.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 37:

﴿And construct the ship﴾ the ark ﴿under Our eyes﴾ within Our sight and protection ﴿and Our inspiration﴾ Our command ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾ who disbelieved, by asking that they not be destroyed

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 38:

﴿And he was constructing the ship﴾, a narration of a past state. ﴿And whenever a group (malaʾ) of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾, they ridiculed him. ﴿He said: If you mock us, then we will mock you just as you mock﴾, when we are saved and you drown.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 11, verse 39:

﴿So you will soon know who it is that will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and descend upon him a lasting punishment﴾ "Man" (مَن) is a relative pronoun (مَوْصُولَة) serving as the object of the verb "to know" (العِلْم). ﴿Will receive a punishment that disgraces him and descends upon him (يَحِلّ) — i.e., will descend (يَنْزِل)﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 40:

﴿Until﴾ is the limit of the crafting, ﴿when Our command came﴾ to destroy them, ﴿and the oven gushed forth﴾ with water for the baker, and that was a sign for Nuh. ﴿We said: Load therein﴾ into the ship ﴿of every kind two﴾ male and female, meaning of every species of them, ﴿two﴾ a male and a female. The word "two" is the object. It is related in the story that Allah gathered for Nuh the beasts, the birds and others, and he began to strike with his hands at every kind, so that his right hand fell upon the male and his left upon the female, and he would load them into the ship. ﴿And your family﴾ meaning his wife and his children ﴿except him against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ meaning among them, by destruction, and that is his wife and his son Kan'an, unlike Sam, Ham and Yafith. So he carried them and their three wives. ﴿And those who believed,﴾ and ﴿none believed with him except a few.﴾ It was said they were six men and their wives. It was also said: all who were in the ship were eighty, half of them men and half of them women.

﴿And he said﴾ Noah. ﴿Embark in it; in the name of God is its running and its anchoring﴾. Both mīms, with fatḥa and with ḍamma, are maṣdars (verbal nouns, *maṣdar*: the verbal noun form of an action), meaning its running (*jaryuhā*) and its anchoring (*rasūhā*), i.e., the end of its course (*muntahā sayrihā*). ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, in that He did not destroy us.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 42:

﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains﴾ in height and magnitude. ﴿And Noah called out to his son﴾ Kan'an, ﴿and he was in a separate place﴾ away from the ship.

﴿He said, "I will betake myself to a mountain that will protect me"﴾ — that will prevent me — ﴿"from the water." He said, "There is no protector today from the command of Allah"﴾ — His punishment — ﴿"except"﴾ — but — ﴿"for him on whom He has mercy."﴾ Allah has mercy on him, so he is the one who is protected.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 44:

﴿And it was said: "O earth, swallow your water,"﴾ the water that gushed out from you, so it drank it, apart from what had descended from the sky, and it became rivers and seas; ﴿and "O sky, withhold,"﴾ hold back from the rain, so it withheld. ﴿And the water subsided﴾ decreased; ﴿and the matter was decided﴾ the affair of the destruction of the people of Noah was completed; ﴿and it (the ship) came to rest﴾ the ship stopped; ﴿on al-Judi﴾ a mountain in the island (al-Jazirah) near Mosul; ﴿and it was said: "Away with"﴾ destruction for ﴿the wrongdoing people﴾, the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 45:

﴿And Noah called out to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family"﴾ — Kan'an — ﴿and indeed Your promise is the truth﴾ — that which will not be broken — ﴿and You are the most just of judges﴾ — the most knowing of them and the most just of them.

﴿قالَ﴾ The Exalted said: ﴿O Noah, he is not of your family﴾, meaning, of those who are saved, or of your religion. ﴿Indeed he﴾, that is, your asking Me for his salvation, ﴿is unrighteous conduct﴾, for he is a disbeliever, and there is no salvation for the disbelievers. In one recitation (qira'a, a canonically transmitted variant), the mim of ﴿عَمِلَ﴾ is pronounced with a kasra, making it the past-tense verb ʿamila, and ﴿غَيْر﴾ is in the accusative (naṣb). The pronoun then refers to his son. ﴿So do not ask Me﴾, with tashdid (doubling of the letter) and with takhfif (its absence), ﴿about that of which you have no knowledge﴾, namely the saving of your son. ﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾ by asking about what you do not know.
﴿He said, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You"﴾ from ﴿asking You for that of which I have no knowledge; and unless You forgive me﴾ what has passed from me (of wrongdoing).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 48:

﴿It was said: "O Noah, descend﴾ (ihbit), i.e., come down from the ship ﴿in peace﴾, i.e., in safety, or with greeting ﴿from Us, and blessings﴾, i.e., goodness ﴿upon you and upon the nations (umam) of those with you﴾ in the ship, i.e., from their offspring and descendants, and they are the believers. ﴿And nations﴾ (read with a nominative ending, wa-umamun) ﴿of those with you﴾. ﴿We shall give them enjoyment﴾ in this world ﴿then a painful punishment will touch them from Us﴾ in the Hereafter, and they are the disbelievers.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 49:

﴿Tilka﴾ i.e., these verses containing the story of Noah ﴿are among the news of the unseen﴾, reports of what was hidden from you, ﴿which We reveal to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿neither you nor your people knew them before this﴾, the Qur'an. ﴿So be patient﴾ in conveying the message and in bearing the harm of your people, as Noah was patient. ﴿Indeed, the final outcome﴾ praiseworthy one, belongs to the righteous.

And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud. [We sent] to 'Ad their brother, from among their tribe, Hud. He said: "O my people, worship Allah," i.e., make Him one. "You have no god other than Him," in which "min" is extra. "You are not, in your worship of idols, but inventors of lies," i.e., liars against Allah.
O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it (i.e., for the monotheism), ﴿ajran﴾ (any wage); ﴿in﴾ (is not) ﴿ajriya illa ʿala alladhi fataranī﴾ (my reward except from the One who created me).

O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord [for shirk] and then turn back to Him [return to Him in obedience]. He will send the sky [rain] upon you in abundance [frequent in its pouring], and He will increase you in strength [in addition to] your strength [through wealth and children]. And do not turn away as criminals [polytheists].
﴿They said, "O Hud, you have brought us no clear proof"﴾, meaning, evidence for what you say, ﴿"and we will not abandon our gods because of your word"﴾, meaning, because of what you say.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 54:

﴿In﴾ (it is only that) we say ﴿naqulu﴾ concerning you ﴿illa i'tarak﴾ (except that) some of our gods have afflicted you ﴿ba'ḍu ālihatinā bisū'in﴾ (some of our gods) with harm, ﴿fa-khabalaka﴾ (and so has deranged you) because of your reviling of them, ﴿fa-anta tahdhī﴾ (so you are raving). ﴿Qāla innī ush-hidu Allāh﴾ (He said: I call God to witness) against me, ﴿wa-ashhadu annī barī'un mimmā tushrikūn﴾ (and bear witness that I am free of what you associate) ﴿tushrikūnahu bihi﴾ (with Him, as you associate) [others] with Him.
﴿Besides Him, so scheme against me﴾ devise my destruction ﴿all together﴾ you and your idols ﴿and then give me no respite﴾ grant me no delay.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 56:

﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature that crawls [upon the earth] except that He holds its forelock.﴾ [The word] ﴿مَا مِنْ﴾ (min) here is extra (zā'idah, i.e., emphatic/superfluous in grammar). ﴿Dābbah﴾ means a living soul (nasamah) that creeps upon the earth. ﴿Illā Huwa ākhidhun bi-nāṣiyatihā﴾ means: He is its Owner (mālikuhā) and its Subduer (qāhiruhā), so there is no benefit and no harm except by His permission. He specified the forelock for mention because whoever has his forelock seized is in a state of utmost humiliation. ﴿Inna Rabbī ʿalā ṣirāṭin mustaqīm﴾ means: upon the path (ṭarīq) of truth and justice.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 57:

﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ There is an elision in it of one of the two tāʾs, meaning: ﴿if you turn away﴾ (tawallaw, i.e., tatawallaw, you turn away) ﴿then I have already conveyed to you what I was sent with to you. And my Lord will bring in place of you a people other than you, and you will not harm Him at all﴾ by your associating [others with Him]. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is, over all things, Guardian﴾ (ḥafīẓ), Watchful (raqīb).
﴿When Our command came﴾, meaning Our punishment, ﴿We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy﴾, meaning guidance, ﴿from Us, and We saved them from a harsh punishment﴾, meaning severe.

Quran verses are in ﴿ ﴾ markers, so I'll translate them plainly inside those markers.

"And that was ʿĀd" — a reference to their remains; that is, travel through the land and look at them. Then it describes their condition, saying: ﴿They denied the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers﴾ — stated in the plural because whoever disobeys one messenger disobeys all the messengers, since they share the same foundation of what they brought, which is tawhid (affirming the oneness of God). ﴿And they followed﴾ — that is, the lowly ones — ﴿the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾, one who opposes the truth, from among their leaders.

And they were followed by a curse in this world (from the people) and on the Day of Resurrection (a curse before all creation). Indeed, ʿĀd disbelieved (denied) their Lord. Ah, away with ʿĀd (a distance from the mercy of God).

And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih, from among their own people. He said: ﴿O my people, worship Allah [i.e., affirm His oneness]. You have no god other than Him. He produced you from the earth [i.e., by creating your father Adam from it], and made you settlers in it [i.e., made you its inhabitants, dwelling in it]. So seek His forgiveness [from shirk (associating partners with Allah)], then turn back to Him [return to Him] in obedience.﴾ Indeed my Lord is near [to His creation through His knowledge], responsive to whoever asks Him.

They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of hopes, before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped? Indeed we are in grave doubt about what you call us to, a disquieting doubt."

Expanded for clarity, following the commentary:

﴿They said: O Salih, you were among us one in whom we placed our hopes﴾ — we hoped that you would become a leader — ﴿before this﴾, meaning before what has come from you, ﴿Do you forbid us that we worship what our fathers worshipped?﴾ — of the idols — ﴿And indeed we are in doubt concerning that to which you call us﴾ — of monotheism (tawhid) — ﴿disquieting﴾, that is, one causing suspicion (rayb).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 63:

﴿He said: "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself"﴾ — clear proof from my Lord, and He has given me mercy — prophethood — ﴿then who will support me against Allah﴾ — who will prevent me from Allah, that is, His punishment — ﴿if I disobey Him? You would only add to me loss﴾ — by your command to me to do so — ﴿other than ruin﴾ — misguidance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 64:

﴿And O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah, as a sign for you⟩ "this" is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), its governing element being the demonstrative (al-ishāra); ﴿so leave her to eat in the land of Allah, and do not touch her with harm⟩ meaning hamstringing (ʿaqr); ﴿lest a near punishment seize you⟩ if you hamstring her.

﴿So they hamstrung her﴾. Qidar hamstrung her at their command. ﴿Then he said﴾, Salih, ﴿"Enjoy yourselves﴾, live, ﴿in your homes for three days﴾. Then you will perish. ﴿That is a promise not to be denied﴾ in it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 11, verse 66:

﴿So when Our command came﴾ to destroy them, ﴿We saved Salih and those who believed with him﴾ — and they were four thousand — ﴿by a mercy from Us﴾ We saved them ﴿and from the disgrace of that Day.﴾ The meem in "yawmi'idhin" is kasra in terms of i'rab (grammatical inflection), and fatha as a fixed form (bina') because it is attached to a built (mabni) noun, which is the more common reading. ﴿Indeed, your Lord — He is the Strong, the Mighty﴾ — the Overpowering.
﴿And those who did wrong were seized by the Cry, so they were in their homes fallen prostrate﴾, kneeling on their knees, dead.

﴿Ka'anna﴾ is the light (mukhaffafah) form, and its subject is omitted; the meaning is ﴿ka'annahum﴾ ("as if they"). ﴿Lam yaghnaw﴾ means they did not dwell or live ﴿fīhā﴾ in it, that is, in their homes. ﴿Alā inna Thamūda kafarū Rabbahum. Alā bu'dan li-Thamūd﴾ means: "Behold, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. Behold, away with Thamud!" The name is pronounced with tanwin and without it, according to whether it is understood as referring to the tribe (qabīlah) or to the living group (ḥayy).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 69:

﴿And our messengers came to Ibrahim with the good news﴾ of Ishaq and, after him, Ya'qub. ﴿They said, "Salaman."﴾ It is a verbal noun (masdar) [of a suppressed verb]. ﴿He said, "Salamun"﴾ upon you. ﴿Then he did not delay to bring a roasted calf (ʿijl ḥanīdh)﴾ that was grilled.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 70:

﴿When he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he disliked them﴾, meaning he found them repugnant (nakirahum, from inkara) ﴿and he harboured fear of them﴾, he concealed within himself ﴿fear﴾, a fear ﴿They said: "Do not fear; we have been sent to the people of Lut"﴾ to destroy them.

﴿And his wife﴾, that is, the wife of Ibrahim, Sarah, ﴿was standing﴾, serving them, ﴿so she laughed﴾ out of joy at their destruction. ﴿So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾, his son, who would live until she saw him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 72:

﴿She said: "Woe to me!"﴾ (ويلتى) is a phrase said at the occurrence of a great matter, and the alif is substituted for the ya' of possession (ya' al-idafa). ﴿Shall I give birth while I am an old woman?﴾ I am ninety-nine years old. ﴿And this, my husband, is an old man﴾ he is a hundred, or a hundred and twenty years old, and it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), and the governing element in it is the demonstrative meaning contained in "dha" (this). ﴿Indeed, this is an amazing thing!﴾ that a child should be born to two decrepit elders.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 73:

﴿They said: "Do you wonder at the command of Allah?﴾ That is, at His power. ﴿The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house﴾ — O people of the house of Ibrahim. ﴿Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious﴾ — praiseworthy, glorious, generous.

﴿When the fear had gone from Abraham﴾, meaning the fright, ﴿and the good news had come to him﴾, meaning of the son, ﴿he began to argue with Us﴾, meaning he began to argue with Our messengers ﴿concerning﴾ the matter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 75:

﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was forbearing﴾, abundant in patience, ﴿supplicating and turning back [to Allah]﴾, returning [to Him] repeatedly. He said to them, "Will you destroy a town in which there are three hundred believers?" They said, "No." He said, "Will you destroy a town in which there are two hundred believers?" They said, "No." He said, "Will you destroy a town in which there are forty believers?" They said, "No." He said, "Will you destroy a town in which there are fourteen believers?" They said, "No." He said, "Then what do you think: if there were one believer in it?" They said, "No." He said, "Indeed, in it is Lut." They said, "We know best who is in it," etc.
So when he prolonged his dispute with them, they said: ﴿O Ibrahim, turn away from this﴾ (i.e., from the argument) ﴿for the command of your Lord has come﴾ (i.e., for their destruction).

When Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt helpless for them (ḍāqa bihim dhar'an), lit. his chest constricted, because they were handsome in appearance, in the form of guests, and he feared for them from his people. And he said, "This is a trying day," meaning severe.

﴿And his people came to him﴾ when they learned of them, ﴿rushing﴾ hastening ﴿towards him. And before this﴾ before their coming, ﴿they had been doing the evil deeds﴾ which is intercourse with men in the anus. ﴿He said﴾ Lut, ﴿O my people, these are my daughters﴾ so marry them, ﴿they are purer for you. So fear God and do not disgrace me﴾ shame me ﴿regarding my guests﴾ my guests. ﴿Is there not among you a man of sound judgment?﴾ who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 79:

﴿They said: "You certainly know that we have no need of your daughters, and you surely know what we want."﴾ [i.e., need, ḥājah] ﴿and you surely know what we want﴾ [i.e., of mounting men (ityān al-rijāl)]

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 80:

﴿He said: "If only I had strength against you, or could take refuge in a mighty support"﴾ [i.e., power (ṭāqa)] ﴿or could take refuge in a mighty support﴾ [i.e., a clan (ʿashīra) that would defend me], "I would have attacked you"; ﴿then when the angels saw that﴾

They said, "O Lut, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So travel with your family during a portion of the night, and let none of you look back, except your wife; indeed, what strikes them will strike her too. Their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?"

(Commentary) "So travel with your family during a portion (qit'in, a part) of the night": a portion of the night. "And let none of you look back (yaltafit, turn around to look)": so that he would not see the great punishment that would descend upon them. "Except your wife": it is read in the nominative (marfu') as a substitute (badal) for "anyone," and in another reading in the accusative (mansub) as an exception from "your family," meaning: do not travel with her. "Indeed, what strikes them will strike her too": it is said that he did not take her out with him; it is also said that she went out and looked back, and said, "O my people!" Then a stone came to her and killed her. He asked them about the time of their destruction, and they said, "Indeed their appointed time is the morning." He said, "I would like it to be sooner than that." They said, "Is not the morning near?"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 82:

﴿So when Our command came﴾ to destroy them, ﴿We made its highest part its lowest﴾, i.e., their towns, ﴿and rained upon them stones of baked clay﴾, clay baked by fire, ﴿layered﴾, i.e., in succession.

"Marked" (musawwama): marked, bearing upon them the names of those they are to be hurled at. "With your Lord" ('inda rabbika): this is an adverbial complement (zarf) modifying it. "And it is not" far from the wrongdoers: the stones, or their cities, [are not far] from the wrongdoers, i.e., the people of Mecca.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 11, verse 84:

﴿And﴾ We sent ﴿to Madyan their brother Shu'ayb﴾. He said: "O my people, worship ﴿Allah﴾" (uwhhidūhu, i.e., declare Him one), ﴿you have no god other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the scale﴾. "Indeed, I see you in ﴿prosperity﴾" (ni'mah, a blessing that makes you independent of cheating in measure, al-taṭfīf), ﴿and indeed I fear for you﴾ if you do not believe ﴿the punishment of an encompassing day﴾ that will encompass you and destroy you. Describing the day as "encompassing" is a metaphor (majāz), since the punishment occurs within it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 85:

﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight⁠ ﴾ — complete them ﴿with justice⁠﴾ — with equity ﴿and do not deprive people of their due⁠﴾ — do not diminish anything of their right ﴿and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption⁠﴾ — by killing and other than it. ʿathā (to commit abuse, a verb whose ʿayn is vowelled with kasra in its form ʿathiya) means "he corrupted." The word mufsidīn (spreading corruption) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) emphasizing the meaning of its governing verb, taʿthaw.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 86:

﴿What remains for you of Allah's provision﴾, His lasting sustenance that remains for you after giving full measure and weight, ﴿is better for you﴾ than diminishing (people's goods). ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾, a watcher who will requite you for your deeds. Indeed, I was sent only as a warner.

They said, mockingly, to him: "O Shu'ayb! Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped (of the idols), or that we cease doing with our wealth what we wish?" The meaning: this is a false matter, to which no one calls with good. "Indeed you are the forbearing, the rightly guided!" They said that mockingly.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, the exegesis (tafsir, "explanation") of the two Jalals) on surah 11, verse 88:**

﴿He said: "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear proof from my Lord, and He has given me good provision"﴾ [lawful (ḥalāl)]. "Shall I then mix it with the unlawful (ḥarām) of defrauding (al-bakhs) and cheating in measure (al-taṭfīf)?" ﴿"And I do not intend to oppose you"﴾ and go off ﴿"to that which I forbid you from"﴾ and commit it. ﴿"I intend only reform"﴾ for you, through justice, ﴿"as far as I am able. And my success is not except through Allah. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn back"﴾ [return].

﴿And O my people, let not my opposition bring upon you﴾ [the same fate]. The verb *yajrimannakum* means *yaksibannakum* (earns you, brings upon you). *Shiqaqi* means *khilafi* (my opposing). The grammatical subject (*fa'il*) of *yajrim* is *shiqaqi*, and the attached pronoun *kum* is the first object (*maf'ul awwal*). The second object is *an yusibakum mithla ma asaba qawma Nuh aw qawma Hud aw qawma Salih* ﴿that there befall you the like of what befell the people of Nuh, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih﴾ of the punishment. ﴿And the people of Lut are not far from you﴾, meaning their dwellings, or the time of their destruction. So take warning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 90:

﴿And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful﴾ to the believers ﴿Affectionate﴾ loving toward them.

"They said" — signalling their indifference: "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say. And indeed we see you among us as weak," humiliated. "And were it not for your clan," your tribe, "we would have stoned you," with stones. "And you are not honoured over us," dear/esteemed such that we would refrain from stoning you. Rather, your clan are the ones who are honoured.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 92:

﴿He said: "O my people, is my clan more esteemed by you than Allah?"﴾ So you abandon killing me for their sake, and you do not protect me for the sake of Allah. ﴿And you have taken Him⦅i.e., Allah⦆ ﴿behind your backs as something cast away﴾, cast behind your backs, not heeding Him. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do﴾ in knowledge, so He will repay you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 93:

﴿And O my people, act according to your standing﴾ i.e., your state, ﴿indeed I am acting [according to mine]﴾ i.e., according to my state. ﴿You will know who﴾ (mawsulah, relative pronoun, being the object of the verb "to know") ﴿will receive a punishment that will disgrace him, and who is a liar. And wait﴾ i.e., await the outcome of your affair, ﴿indeed I am with you, a watcher﴾ i.e., awaiting.

﴿When Our command came﴾ to destroy them, ﴿We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the blast seized those who did wrong﴾. Jibril (Gabriel) cried out at them. ﴿So they were found in their homes, fallen prostrate﴾, kneeling on their knees and dead.

﴿As if﴾ (كَأَنْ) is *mukhaffafa* (the lightened form of *ka'anna*, in which the particle's emphasis is reduced), meaning: ﴿as if they﴾ (أيْ كَأَنَّهُمْ) ﴿had not lived﴾ (لَمْ يَغْنَوْا), meaning ﴿they had not dwelt﴾ (يُقِيمُوا).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 96:

﴿And We certainly sent Musa with Our signs and a clear authority﴾ — a clear, manifest proof.
﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs. But they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right guidance.﴾ *sadid* (sound, correct)

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 11, verse 98:

﴿Yaqdumu﴾ (he will go before): yatqaddam (he will precede) ﴿qawmahu yawm al-qiyamah﴾ (his people on the Day of Resurrection), so they will follow him as they followed him in the world. ﴿Fa-awradahum﴾ (and he will bring them down): adkhalahum (he will cause them to enter) ﴿al-nar﴾ (the Fire). ﴿Wa-bi'sa al-wirdu al-mawrud﴾ (And wretched is the watering place to which they are brought): hiya (it is).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 99:

﴿And they were followed by a curse in this [world], and on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — i.e., in this world, ﴿a curse﴾ — ﴿wretched is the gift [rifd] that is given﴾ — the aid (al-'awn) ﴿that is given﴾ — their gift.

﴿That﴾, the aforementioned, is a *mubtada'* (grammatical subject) whose *khabar* (predicate) is ﴿from the news of the towns, which We relate to you﴾, O Muhammad. ﴿Some of them﴾, i.e., of the towns, ﴿are standing﴾, their people having perished while the town itself remains. ﴿And some are harvested﴾: ﴿and some of them are harvested﴾, their people having perished along with them, so no trace of them remains, like crops cut down with sickles.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 101:

﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ by destroying them without a sin, ﴿but they wronged themselves﴾ by associating partners with God. ﴿So their gods, which they called upon besides God, availed them nothing﴾ (lit. "did not avail," i.e., did not repel) ﴿of anything when the command of your Lord came﴾ — His punishment. ﴿And they added nothing to them﴾ by their worshipping them ﴿except ruin﴾ (i.e., loss).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 102:

﴿And thus﴾ like that seizure, ﴿is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns﴾ meaning their inhabitants, ﴿while they are wrongdoers﴾ through their sins; that is, none of their possessions will avail them against His seizure. ﴿Indeed His seizure is painful, severe.﴾ Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not release him." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And thus is the seizure of your Lord﴾ [to the end of the verse].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 103:

﴿Indeed in that﴾ mentioned in the stories ﴿is surely a sign﴾ a lesson ﴿for him who fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That﴾ i.e., the Day of Resurrection ﴿is a Day for which mankind will be gathered﴾ in it ﴿and that is a Day witnessed﴾ witnessed by all creatures.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 104:

﴿And We do not delay it except for a term already counted.﴾ (for a time known with Allah)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 105:

﴿On the Day it comes﴾ that day, ﴿no soul shall speak﴾ here one of the two tā' (tāʾān) is elided, i.e. "tatakallamu" becomes "takallamu," ﴿except by His permission﴾ the Exalted's. ﴿Among them﴾ i.e. among the creation, ﴿there are wretched﴾ ﴿and﴾ among them ﴿happy﴾; each was written in the pre-eternity (al-azal).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 106:

﴿As for those who are wretched﴾ in His knowledge, ﴿they will be in the Fire, for them therein will be groaning﴾ a loud sound ﴿and wailing﴾ a faint sound.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 107:

﴿Abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: i.e., for the duration of their enduring in the world. ﴿Except﴾ other than ﴿what your Lord wills﴾ of an addition beyond their duration, which has no end. The meaning is: abiding therein forever.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 108:

﴿And as for those who were made happy﴾ (with the vowel on the sīn read as fatḥa or ḍamma), ﴿they will be in the Garden, abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except﴾ (other than) ﴿what your Lord wills﴾, as has been explained before, and what is indicated concerning them by His saying ﴿a gift not cut off﴾: a gift ﴿not cut off﴾, i.e., unending. And the interpretation mentioned earlier is the one that has become clear, and it is free of artificiality. And God knows best His intended meaning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 109:

﴿So do not be﴾ O Muhammad ﴿in doubt﴾ (shakk) ﴿about what these worship﴾ of idols, ﴿[for] we will surely punish them as We punished those before them.﴾ This is a consolation for the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿They worship only as their fathers worshipped before﴾, i.e., like their worship ﴿before﴾, and We had punished them. ﴿And indeed, We will give them their full share﴾ like them, their portion ﴿of punishment﴾ (ḥaẓẓ min al-ʿadhāb) ﴿without reduction﴾, i.e., complete.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 110:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾ — the Torah — ﴿but it was disputed about﴾ — with affirmation and denial, like the Qur'an — ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ — by delaying the reckoning and the recompense for creation until the Day of Resurrection — ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾ — in this world — ﴿concerning that about which they differ﴾. ﴿And indeed they﴾ — that is, those who deny it — ﴿are in disquieting doubt about it﴾ — causing suspicion.

﴿وإنْ﴾ (wa-in), read with light (takhfif) and emphatic (tashdid) pronunciation, ﴿كُلًّا﴾ (kullan), i.e., all creatures. ﴿لَمّا﴾ (lammā): the ﴿ما﴾ is extra (zā'idah), and the lām is either a preparatory lām (muwaṭṭi'ah) for an implied oath (qasam muqaddar), or a distinguishing lām (fāriqah). In one recitation (qirā'ah), ﴿لَمّا﴾ is read with tashdid, meaning ﴿إلّا﴾ (illā, "except"), and then ﴿إنْ﴾ is negative. ﴿لَيُوَفِّيَنهمْ رَبّك أعْمالهمْ﴾: that is, your Lord will surely repay them in full for their deeds, i.e., their recompense (jazā'ahā). ﴿إنّهُ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ خَبِير﴾: He is All-Aware of what they do, knowing their inner states (bawāṭinihi) as well as their outward actions (ẓawāhirihi).

﴿So be steadfast﴾ in acting upon your Lord's command and in calling to Him, ﴿as you have been commanded﴾, and let those who have repented along with you [i.e., believed] be steadfast with you. ﴿And do not transgress﴾, that is, do not exceed the limits of God. ﴿Indeed He is Seeing of what you do﴾, so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 113:

﴿And do not incline﴾ (tamīlū) toward ﴿those who have wronged﴾ (zalamū), out of affection, or flattery, or approval of their deeds, ﴿lest the Fire touch you﴾ (tuṣībakum), ﴿and you have no protectors other than Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿from﴾ (min is extra here) ﴿protectors﴾ who would guard you from Him, ﴿then you will not be helped﴾ (tumna'ūna), i.e., you will not be prevented from His punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 114:

﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾ — al-ghadah (the morning) and al-‘ashiyy (the evening), i.e., the Subh (dawn prayer), the Zuhr (midday prayer) and the ‘Asr (afternoon prayer). ﴿And at the approaches of the night﴾ — zulafan is the plural of zulfah, meaning a portion, ﴿of the night﴾: the Maghrib (sunset prayer) and the ‘Isha’ (night prayer). ﴿Indeed, good deeds﴾ — such as the five prayers — ﴿remove misdeeds﴾, meaning minor sins. It was revealed concerning a man who kissed a non-related woman, and the Prophet (ﷺ) informed him. He said, "Is this for me?" He (ﷺ) said, "For all of my nation, entirely." Narrated by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim). ﴿That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ — an admonition for those who take heed.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 11, verse 115:

﴿And be patient﴾ O Muhammad, over the harm of your people, or over the prayer, ﴿for indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good﴾ through patience in obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 116:

﴿Why were there not﴾ (fa-lawla, i.e. fa-hallā: "why not"), among the generations ﴿before you﴾, the past nations, ﴿people of virtue (ūlū baqiyya)﴾ meaning people of religion and excellence, ﴿who would forbid corruption on earth﴾. The meaning here is negation: that is, there were not among them such people. ﴿Except﴾ (illā: "but" in the sense of "however") ﴿a few of those We saved from among them﴾, who forbade it and were saved. The min here is explanatory (li-l-bayān). ﴿And those who did wrong﴾ by corruption and by abandoning the forbidding ﴿followed what they had been given in luxury﴾, i.e. they enjoyed comfort.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 117:

﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾ on His part toward them, ﴿while their people were reforming﴾ [i.e., were] believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 118:

﴿And had your Lord willed, He would have made mankind one community﴾ (i.e., people of one religion), ﴿but they continue to differ﴾ concerning the religion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 119:

﴿Except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾ — He willed good for them, so they do not differ concerning it. ﴿And for that He created them﴾ — i.e., the people of disagreement for it (ikhtilaf, "difference of opinion") and the people of mercy for it. ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾ — and it is:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 120:

﴿And all⟩ is in the accusative by [the verb] "naqussu" (We relate), and its tanwin is a substitute for the genitive noun that was omitted (i.e., kullu mā yaḥtāju ilayhi, "everything that he needs").

﴿We relate to you from the news of the messengers that⟩ is a substitute (badal) for "kullan." ﴿with it We make firm⟩ — nuṭammin (We reassure) — ﴿your heart⟩ — qalbaka (your heart). ﴿And there has come to you in this⟩ — [i.e., in these reports] or [in these] verses — ﴿the truth, and an admonition and a reminder for the believers.⟩ They were singled out for mention because they benefit from them in faith, unlike the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 11, verse 121:

﴿And say to those who do not believe: "Act according to your position [on your way]﴾ (ḥālatikum), ﴿indeed we are acting [according to ours]﴾ (ʿalā ḥālatinā). It is a threat to them.
﴿And wait﴾ for the outcome of your affair, ﴿indeed we are waiting﴾ for that.

To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, i.e., the knowledge of what is hidden in them, and to Him the whole matter is returned, (read with the active verb) "yaʿūd" (it returns), or (with the passive) "yuradd" (it is brought back), so He will take vengeance on those who disobeyed. So worship Him alone, and put your trust in Him, rely on Him, for He is sufficient for you. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do; He only delays them until their appointed time. And in one reading it is with the second-person ("taʿmalūn" with the ta').
